changelog.change: Initial entry — the pARC logistic model built as an interactive calculator from the published coefficients (Kharbanda 2018 / NCT02633735 SAP). Age/sex group is a single pre-resolved select; the ANC term uses min(1.77·√ANC, 6.62), which is identical to the paper's piecewise definition since 1.77·√14 = 6.62.

purpose: Continuous, individualized probability of appendicitis in a child 5-18 years with < 96 h of pain. Unlike Alvarado and PAS this is a regression model, not a point score — it outputs a percent risk and is the most decision-actionable of the three for the imaging decision when an absolute neutrophil count is available.
ageRange: Children 5-18 years, pain < 96 h (not validated outside this range)

embeddedCalculator.title: Pediatric Appendicitis Risk Calculator (pARC)
sources: Appy-CDS Manual of Operations v19 / NCT02633735 SAP (coefficient table)
embeddedCalculator.purpose: pARC logistic regression → percent probability of appendicitis.

inputs.label: History of pain migration to the RLQ

formulas.label: pARC — probability of appendicitis
formulas.expression: 100 / (1 + exp(-(-8.7 + ageSex + duration + walking + migration + tenderness + guarding + min(1.77 * sqrt(anc), 6.62))))

interpretation.label: < 5% — very low risk. Appendicitis very unlikely; discharge with return precautions and follow-up is generally reasonable without imaging.
5-14% — low risk. Consider observation and serial exams over imaging; ultrasound if suspicion persists.
15-24% — low-intermediate risk. Ultrasound first-line; observation / repeat exam an alternative.
25-49% — intermediate risk. Ultrasound; surgical involvement as indicated by the study and course.
50-74% — high-intermediate risk. Ultrasound and surgical consultation; CT or MRI if ultrasound is non-diagnostic.
75-84% — high risk (validation cohort: ~2.6% negative-pathology rate). Surgical consultation; imaging often still obtained to confirm.
≥ 85% — highest risk (validation cohort: ~1.2% negative-pathology rate, ~99.7% specificity). Surgical consultation; some centres proceed without further imaging.

embeddedCalculator.notes: Model: z = -8.7 + (age/sex term) + (duration term) + 1.05·walking + 0.46·migration + 1.14·RLQ-tenderness + 0.67·guarding + min(1.77·√ANC, 6.62); probability = 100 ÷ (1 + e^−z). ANC in ×10³/µL (= ×10⁹/L). If only WBC is available: ANC ≈ (−0.8783 + 1.1008·√WBC)² (WBC in ×10³/µL); if neither, the derivation used ANC = 7. The min(…, 6.62) cap is exactly the paper's piecewise rule because 1.77·√14 = 6.62. Coefficients are from the Kharbanda 2018 / NCT02633735 SAP coefficient table; the female age-8 band upper bound is taken as 12 y from the model's reference group ("Male 14-18 / Female 12-18"). Cross-check MDCalc for borderline values. NOT validated below 5 y or beyond 96 h of pain, or in pregnancy, IBD, prior abdominal surgery, or cystic fibrosis.
embeddedCalculator.buildNote: Formula engine. Age/sex is one pre-resolved select (each option's value = male-main 1.28 + age-main ± the male×[5-7.9] interaction −1.05, per the SAP table). ANC piecewise encoded as min(1.77·√ANC, 6.62). Seven risk bands per the paper's clinically actionable categories.

body.text: pARC is a regression model, not a point score. Enter the seven inputs and read the percent risk. It needs an absolute neutrophil count — if you only have a WBC, the ANC imputation is in the notes. Validated only for children 5-18 years with < 96 h of pain.

rows: Low-tech / outpatient settings with limited labs
Fast ED first-pass when suspicion is already high
The individualized imaging decision in kids ≥ 5 when an ANC is available

body.text: In the validation cohort pARC confidently classified nearly half of patients as clearly low-risk (< 15%) or clearly high-risk (≥ 85%), versus ~23% for a comparably confident PAS cutoff (< 3 or > 8). AUC 0.85 (Kharbanda 2018) to 0.89 (Cotton 2019, community EDs).
probability (%) = 100 ÷ (1 + e^−z), where z is the sum of the applicable terms.

A low pARC does not rule appendicitis out in a child whose exam is worsening — it is one input. Do not apply it below 5 years (appendicitis is rarer and more atypical there) or beyond 96 h of pain, or in pregnancy, IBD, prior abdominal surgery, or cystic fibrosis. For the point-score alternative see the Pediatric Appendicitis Score.

buildNote: peds-tool with an embedded formula calculator (+ explanatory body — web renderPedsTool now renders both). Coefficients reproduced from the Kharbanda 2018 model as published in the NCT02633735 SAP coefficient table. One interpretive assumption is documented: the female age band upper bound of 12 y (from the model's reference group). Companion to `pediatric-appendicitis-score`; `alvarado` cross-links both.
